absolute frequency

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure representing the total number of occurrences of a specific item within a defined dataset. This concept is essential for statistical analysis, as it serves as a foundational element for calculating relative frequencies and comparing observed data against expected frequencies in various contexts. Absolute frequency contrasts with relative frequency, which expresses occurrences in relation to the total number of observations.

Definición (ES)

Medida cuantitativa que representa el número total de ocurrencias de un elemento específico dentro de un conjunto de datos definido. Este concepto es fundamental para el análisis estadístico, ya que sirve como elemento base para calcular frecuencias relativas y comparar datos observados con frecuencias esperadas en diversos contextos. La frecuencia absoluta se contrasta con la frecuencia relativa, que expresa las ocurrencias en relación con el número total de observaciones.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • relative frequency — This term represents occurrences in relation to the total number of observations, contrasting with absolute frequency, which counts total occurrences.
  • frequency list — A frequency list compiles absolute frequencies of items, providing a basis for further statistical analysis.
  • observed frequency — Observed frequency refers to the actual counts recorded in data, which can be compared to absolute frequencies for validation.
  • expected frequency — Expected frequency is derived from theoretical models and contrasts with absolute frequency, which is based on actual data.
  • statistical significance — Statistical significance often relies on absolute frequencies to determine the likelihood that observed patterns are not due to chance.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "If we want to convert the absolute frequencies in Table 5.1 into relative frequencies, we first have to decide what the relevant total N is." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

  • "This comparison between observed and expected frequencies also provides a foundation for inferential statistics." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

  • "In determining the ratio, however, we used relative references for both parts of the equation." (2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

  • "The absolute frequencies of the intersections of our variables with the expected absolute frequencies..." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

  • "Frecuencia absoluta Número de documentos Frecuencia normalizada (casos por millón) jugo 6161 2479 21,9 zumo 2673 9,5." (2021_Rojo, G._Introducción a la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • "En un corpus adecuadamente codificado se puede encontrar información no solo sobre la frecuencia, sino también sobre la distribución de una palabra." (2021_Rojo, G._Introducción a la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • "La explotación básica de los corpus peso que suponen los elementos más frecuentes sobre el total..." (2021_Rojo, G._Introducción a la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • "Frecuencia absoluta y frecuencia normalizada en función de su distribución por zonas..." (2022_Sánchez Lancis, C._Corpus diacrónicos del español de España)

  • "Este valor ubica dentro de un continuo o ranking, que va de lo más frecuente en el corpus a lo menos..." (2015_Molina Salinas, C., Sierra Martínez, G. E._Hacia una normalización de la frecuencia de los corpus CREA y CORDE_Signos)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "absolute frequency" is widely used in corpus linguistics to provide a clear count of occurrences, serving as a basis for further statistical analysis. Its distinction from relative frequency is crucial for understanding data representation and analysis in linguistic research.

El término "frecuencia absoluta" se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para proporcionar un conteo claro de ocurrencias, sirviendo como base para un análisis estadístico posterior. Su distinción de la frecuencia relativa es crucial para comprender la representación y el análisis de datos en la investigación lingüística.

accuracy

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A measure of the correctness of data annotation, defined as the proportion of true positive results among all instances identified by a query. This term is crucial in evaluating the quality of corpus data retrieval and annotation, contrasting with recall, which focuses on the completeness of identified instances. High accuracy indicates that the annotation scheme or retrieval method effectively distinguishes between correct and incorrect classifications.

Definición (ES)

Una medida de la corrección de la anotación de datos, definida como la proporción de resultados verdaderamente positivos entre todas las instancias identificadas por una consulta. Este término es fundamental para evaluar la calidad de la recuperación y anotación de datos en corpus, contrastando con el recall, que se centra en la exhaustividad de las instancias identificadas. Una alta precisión indica que el esquema de anotación o el método de recuperación distingue eficazmente entre clasificaciones correctas e incorrectas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • precision — Accuracy is often discussed alongside precision, which measures the proportion of true positives among all positive results returned by a query.
  • recall — Recall contrasts with accuracy by focusing on the completeness of the identified instances rather than the correctness of those identifications.
  • annotation scheme — The effectiveness of an annotation scheme can be evaluated through the accuracy of the annotations it produces.
  • tagger — The accuracy of a tagger is critical in determining how well it assigns correct labels to corpus data.
  • corpus annotation — Accuracy is a key metric in assessing the quality of corpus annotation processes.
  • inter-annotator agreement — High accuracy in annotations can contribute to improved inter-annotator agreement, indicating consistency among different annotators.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "Ideally, the value of both measures should be 1, i.e., our data should include all cases of the phenomenon under investigation (a recall rate of 100 percent) and it should include nothing that is not a case of this phenomenon (a precision of 100 percent)." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

  • "In these more complex cases, we can, and should, assess the quality of the automatic annotation in the same way in which we would assess the quality of the results returned by a particular query, in terms of precision and recall." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

  • "Although the degree of accuracy was higher than expected, especially in the earlier subperiods, we can see that the tagger is less precise with earlier texts." (2017_Fanego, T., Rodríguez-Puente, et al._The Corpus of Historical English Law Reports. A resource for analysis the development of English_ICAME)

  • "Most of the tagging errors made by CLAWS correspond to those potential mistakes typical in any kind of text, such as confusion between after, as, before, since and until as prepositions or subordinating conjunctions." (2017_Fanego, T., Rodríguez-Puente, et al._The Corpus of Historical English Law Reports. A resource for analysis the development of English_ICAME)

  • "El análisis de errores gana en precisión y posibilidades de generalización si el corpus ha recibido ese tipo de codificación." (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)

  • "Los corpus generales permiten, en efecto, extraer datos acerca de las características relevantes de la L2 y hacerlo de forma selectiva en función de los diferentes tipos de texto." (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)

  • "El rasgo más habitualmente destacado de los corpus de aprendientes frente a otros es la posibilidad de indicar también, entre los rasgos incorporados en la codificación, el nivel de conocimientos de la L2." (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)

  • "La precisión de la anotación es un aspecto fundamental que se debe considerar al evaluar la calidad de los corpus." (2022_Davies, M., Parodi, G._Constitución de corpus crecientes del español)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "accuracy" is frequently used in the context of data annotation and retrieval, emphasizing the importance of correct classifications in corpus linguistics. Variations in accuracy can arise based on the complexity of the data being annotated and the methods employed, highlighting the need for careful evaluation of annotation schemes and retrieval processes.

El término "precisión" se utiliza con frecuencia en el contexto de la anotación y recuperación de datos, enfatizando la importancia de las clasificaciones correctas en la lingüística de corpus. Las variaciones en la precisión pueden surgir según la complejidad de los datos que se anotan y los métodos empleados, lo que resalta la necesidad de una evaluación cuidadosa de los esquemas de anotación y los procesos de recuperación.

alignment

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento del lenguaje

Definition (EN)

The process of matching corresponding segments in source and target texts, typically at the sentence level, is essential in the creation of parallel corpora. This methodological approach often requires both automatic tools and manual verification to ensure high-quality alignments, as automatic alignment alone may not account for complexities such as sentence merging or splitting. The term is closely related to the concept of multilingual linguistic annotation, which raises questions about comparability across languages.

Definición (ES)

El proceso de emparejamiento de segmentos correspondientes en textos fuente y meta, generalmente a nivel de oración, es fundamental en la creación de corpus paralelos. Este enfoque metodológico a menudo requiere tanto herramientas automáticas como verificación manual para garantizar alineaciones de alta calidad, ya que la alineación automática por sí sola puede no considerar complejidades como la fusión o división de oraciones. El término está estrechamente relacionado con la anotación lingüística multilingüe, que plantea interrogantes sobre la comparabilidad entre lenguas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • parallel corpus — A parallel corpus is a collection of texts in two languages that are aligned at various levels, making alignment a crucial process for its compilation.
  • annotation — Annotation often accompanies alignment, as it provides additional linguistic information that can enhance the quality of the aligned segments.
  • corpus design — Effective corpus design must consider alignment strategies to ensure that the resulting corpus meets the needs of comparative linguistic analysis.
  • translation memory — Translation memory systems utilize alignment techniques to store and retrieve previously translated segments, highlighting the practical applications of alignment in translation.
  • multilingual corpus — A multilingual corpus requires careful alignment across different languages to maintain the integrity and comparability of the data.
  • manual verification — Manual verification is often necessary in the alignment process to correct errors that automatic tools may introduce, ensuring the reliability of the aligned texts.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "the performance of the individual alignment tools varies for different types of texts and language pairs and in order to guarantee high quality alignments, a manual verification step is needed." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)

  • "Software tools can be used to align parallel texts automatically at paragraph, sentence and word level." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)

  • "Sentence alignment is not a straightforward task, as translators often merge or split sentences when producing the target text." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)

  • "Such rough alignment yields satisfactory results at the sentence level, especially when it is supported by various statistical methods." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

  • "The high quality needed for descriptive translation research can only be obtained through manual alignment editing." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)

  • "una alineación incorrecta desvirtuaría los resultados del corpus en los estudios descriptivos realizados con él." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)

  • "la alineación de corpus paralelos es un proceso demandante y laborioso." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)

  • "la alineación cotejada por párrafos permite una alineación más fluida a nivel de oración." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)

  • "la alineación automática de dos documentos que luego puede revisarse de forma manual." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)

  • "la alineación es fundamental para optimizar el mapeo entre unidades equivalentes." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "alignment" is primarily used in the context of parallel corpora and translation studies, where it plays a critical role in ensuring the accuracy and reliability of linguistic comparisons across languages. Variations in alignment methods, such as automatic versus manual alignment, reflect ongoing debates about the best practices in corpus linguistics.

El término "alineación" se utiliza principalmente en el contexto de los corpus paralelos y los estudios de traducción, donde desempeña un papel crítico en la garantía de la precisión y fiabilidad de las comparaciones lingüísticas entre lenguas. Las variaciones en los métodos de alineación, como la alineación automática frente a la manual, reflejan debates en curso sobre las mejores prácticas en la lingüística de corpus.

annotated corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A collection of texts that includes additional information beyond the raw text, such as linguistic or metalinguistic features. This additional information can encompass markup, part-of-speech tagging, and semantic tagging, which enhance the corpus's utility for linguistic analysis. The methodological approach to annotation varies, with part-of-speech tagging being the most common form, while other types of annotations may include pragmatic or syntactic information.

Definición (ES)

Un conjunto de textos que incluye información adicional más allá del texto en bruto, como características lingüísticas o metalingüísticas. Esta información adicional puede abarcar etiquetado, etiquetado de partes del discurso y etiquetado semántico, lo que aumenta la utilidad del corpus para el análisis lingüístico. El enfoque metodológico para la anotación varía, siendo el etiquetado de partes del discurso la forma más común, mientras que otros tipos de anotaciones pueden incluir información pragmática o sintáctica.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — Annotation is a fundamental component of an annotated corpus, providing the additional linguistic information necessary for analysis.
  • part-of-speech tagging — This is a specific type of annotation commonly found in annotated corpora, essential for grammatical categorization.
  • markup language — Markup languages like XML are often used in the creation of annotated corpora to structure the additional information.
  • corpus design — The design of an annotated corpus involves careful planning to determine the types of annotations that will be included.
  • metadata — Metadata may accompany an annotated corpus, providing contextual information about the data and its collection.
  • semantic annotation — This type of annotation adds layers of meaning to the texts within an annotated corpus, enhancing linguistic analysis.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • A corpus is annotated when it consists of more than the actual words in the document (which is generally known as plain text). (source: 2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • Annotation is a multilayered term that includes (but is not limited to) markup, POS-tagging, and semantic tagging. (source: 2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • Given the predominance of such applications, it comes as no surprise that the most commonly found kind of annotation is part-of-speech tagging. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)

  • Many corpora have begun to feature other kinds of annotation. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)

  • Pragmatically annotated corpora, i.e. corpora that are annotated for speech acts or other pragmatically relevant information, are still relatively rare. (source: 2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

  • Se trata de un corpus de la lengua estándar de la variedad del español peninsular, anotado a distintos niveles: morfosintáctico (categoría gramatical y lema), sintáctico (constituyentes y funciones), semántico (sentidos de WordNet, estructura argumental, roles semánticos y entidades) y pragmático (relaciones de correferencia). (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • El CE está parcialmente anotado y lematizado, lo que facilita la investigación lingüística. (fuente: 2022_Molina Plaza, S._Herramientas, recursos y metodologías de análisis para la traducción mediante corpus lingüísticos del español)

  • Entre los corpus anotados de español de libre distribución destacan los corpus ARTHUS asociado a la base de datos ADESSE. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • AnCora constituye una fuente de información para el análisis lingüístico y se ha utilizado profusamente para desarrollar sistemas de análisis automático a diferentes niveles. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • Muchos de ellos son también orientados a tareas, es decir, tratan temas y dominios relativamente limitados, por lo que a menudo no son muy representativos de la interacción hablada general. (fuente: 2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotated corpus" encompasses a variety of annotation types, reflecting the diverse applications in corpus linguistics. The methodological approaches to annotation are evolving, with increasing attention to pragmatic and semantic dimensions alongside traditional part-of-speech tagging.

El término "corpus anotado" abarca una variedad de tipos de anotación, reflejando las diversas aplicaciones en la lingüística de corpus. Los enfoques metodológicos para la anotación están evolucionando, con una atención creciente a las dimensiones pragmáticas y semánticas junto con el etiquetado tradicional de partes del discurso.

annotation

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A systematic process of enriching linguistic data by adding interpretative information, distinguishing it from markup, which may refer to the physical act of marking text. This practice enhances the corpus's value by allowing for more comprehensive searches and research, as it provides explicit linguistic analysis rather than relying on implicit classifications. The design of annotation systems is often influenced by specific research interests, making it a critical methodological component in corpus linguistics.

Definición (ES)

Un proceso sistemático de enriquecimiento de datos lingüísticos mediante la adición de información interpretativa, que se distingue del marcado, el cual puede referirse al acto físico de marcar un texto. Esta práctica aumenta el valor del corpus al permitir búsquedas y análisis más exhaustivos, ya que proporciona un análisis lingüístico explícito en lugar de depender de clasificaciones implícitas. El diseño de los sistemas de anotación suele estar influenciado por intereses de investigación específicos, lo que lo convierte en un componente metodológico crítico en la lingüística de corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — An annotated corpus is a type of corpus that includes additional interpretative information, enhancing its usability for linguistic research.
  • tagset — The choice of tagset is crucial for annotation, as it determines the categories and labels applied to linguistic data.
  • POS tagging — Part-of-speech tagging is a specific type of annotation that assigns grammatical categories to words in a corpus.
  • metadata — Metadata often accompanies annotations, providing context and additional information about the data being annotated.
  • inter-annotator agreement — This concept is essential for evaluating the reliability of annotations, ensuring that different annotators apply consistent criteria.
  • annotation scheme — An annotation scheme outlines the conventions and guidelines used in the annotation process, influencing the quality and consistency of the annotations.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • Second, the annotation practices need to be documented. This can be done in the form of an annotation manual that outlines the conventions that have been applied in creating a set of annotations and at the same time serves as guidelines for users who intend to implement the annotations themselves on their own corpus data. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • Corpus annotation involves enormous amounts of work. This means that when we decide to use an annotation system or devise one ourselves, we need to make sure that the work is worthwhile, that is, the information we require cannot be extracted in some other way using data that is readily available, such as smarter ways of querying. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • The specific design of annotation systems is codetermined by the specific research interests involved and therefore, we will need to refer to various research projects time and again. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • While the term markup is sometimes used to indicate the physical act of marking specific parts of a text using specific symbols, and, in contrast, annotation may often refer to the interpretative information added, the two may also be used synonymously. (source: 2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

  • That is, annotation “only means undertaking and making explicit a linguistic analysis”. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)

  • Given the complexity and multi-layeredness of linguistic data, this leads to two main desiderata. One is that, as annotation for more and more subjective characteristics becomes more frequent, it is imperative that annotation provides efficient ways for dealing with ambiguous or otherwise problematic data points. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)

  • La anotación de un corpus es un proceso iterativo/cíclico. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • Una vez realizado este proceso en el tiempo que se considere oportuno, es decir, cuando la guía ya no requiere modificaciones y se muestra estable, se pasa a la siguiente fase, la evaluación de la calidad de la anotación. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • Para evaluar la calidad de un corpus anotado el criterio fundamental es la consistencia de los datos anotados, es decir, que todos los anotadores han aplicado el mismo criterio para el mismo problema. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • Una gran tasa de acuerdo demuestra que el proceso de anotación es fiable, pero no necesariamente que la anotación es correcta. (fuente: 2022_Moreno Sandoval, A._Etiquetadores morfosintácticos para corpus en español)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation" encompasses various practices in corpus linguistics, often distinguished from markup by its emphasis on interpretative information. Its application is critical for enhancing the usability of linguistic data, and the methodologies surrounding it are continually evolving as new research interests emerge.

El término "anotación" abarca diversas prácticas en la lingüística de corpus, a menudo diferenciándose del marcado por su énfasis en la información interpretativa. Su aplicación es fundamental para aumentar la usabilidad de los datos lingüísticos, y las metodologías que la rodean están en constante evolución a medida que surgen nuevos intereses de investigación.

annotation scheme

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A structured framework for annotating linguistic data, which delineates specific categories and rules for marking entities, relations, and attributes within a text. This methodological tool is essential for ensuring consistency and clarity in the representation of linguistic phenomena, as evidenced by various systems like the ACE Pilot Format and the GNOME coding scheme. Unlike general annotation, an annotation scheme provides a systematic approach to capturing complex linguistic features, such as coreference and anaphoric relations.

Definición (ES)

Marco estructurado para la anotación de datos lingüísticos que delimita categorías específicas y reglas para marcar entidades, relaciones y atributos dentro de un texto. Este instrumento metodológico es esencial para garantizar la consistencia y la claridad en la representación de fenómenos lingüísticos, como evidencian sistemas como el formato ACE Pilot o el esquema de codificación GNOME. A diferencia de la anotación general, un esquema de anotación proporciona un enfoque sistemático para capturar rasgos lingüísticos complejos, tales como la correferencia y las relaciones anafóricas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — An annotation scheme is a specific type of annotation that provides a structured approach to marking linguistic data.
  • annotated corpus — An annotated corpus is created using an annotation scheme, which defines how the data within the corpus is marked and categorized.
  • markup language — An annotation scheme often employs a markup language to encode the annotations within a text, facilitating data processing and analysis.
  • coreference — Many annotation schemes focus on coreference, providing guidelines for marking entities and their references within a text.
  • entity — An annotation scheme typically includes rules for identifying and categorizing entities mentioned in the text.
  • guidelines — Annotation schemes are often accompanied by guidelines that detail the specific rules and categories to be used during the annotation process.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • The annotation system has two basic facets: (1) it captures the identity of referents mentioned by different referring expressions, (2) it captures various aspects of the anaphoric relation. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • Anaphoric information in APF is organized around entities: all entities annotated in the document are identified with elements, and each mention of entity e is then recorded as a child element of the element for e. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

  • Each mention is annotated with the attribute TYPE, with three possible values: NAM for named entities, NOM for NPs with a common noun as head, and PRO for pronouns. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

  • The ACE guidelines follow a small number of semantic classes considered particularly relevant for information extraction: persons, organizations, locations, geopolitical entities, weapons, and vehicles. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

  • The coding scheme inherits several aspects of the GNOME coding scheme, although with fewer attributes, but adding the ability to annotate discourse deixis. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation scheme" is widely used in corpus linguistics to refer to structured frameworks that guide the annotation process, ensuring consistency and clarity in data representation. Variations in annotation schemes may arise based on the specific linguistic features being analyzed or the goals of the research.

El término "esquema de anotación" se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para referirse a marcos estructurados que guían el proceso de anotación, garantizando consistencia y claridad en la representación de datos. Las variaciones en los esquemas de anotación pueden surgir en función de las características lingüísticas específicas que se analizan o de los objetivos de la investigación.

annotation tools

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

Software applications designed to facilitate the process of adding linguistic labels to textual data, enabling both automated and manual annotation. These tools support various annotation goals, such as parts-of-speech tagging and semantic annotation, and are essential for enhancing the analytical capabilities of corpus linguistics. The corpus indicates a trend towards integrating automated systems with manual annotation processes, highlighting their complementary roles in linguistic research.

Definición (ES)

Aplicaciones informáticas que facilitan el proceso de añadir etiquetas lingüísticas a datos textuales, permitiendo tanto la anotación automática como la manual. Estas herramientas apoyan diversos objetivos de anotación, como el etiquetado de partes del discurso y la anotación semántica, y son esenciales para mejorar las capacidades analíticas de la lingüística de corpus. El corpus indica una tendencia hacia la integración de sistemas automáticos con procesos de anotación manual, destacando sus roles complementarios en la investigación lingüística.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — Annotation tools are used to label and analyze data within a corpus.
  • annotation scheme — Annotation tools often operate based on predefined annotation schemes that dictate how data should be labeled.
  • automated annotation — Many annotation tools provide automated annotation features to streamline the labeling process.
  • manual annotations — Some annotation tools allow for manual annotations, which can complement automated processes.

La lingüística de corpus se reconoce por su orientación metodológica distintiva, centrada en la compilación y explotación de corpus como fuentes primarias de datos.

The term "corpus-driven" is primarily used to describe a methodological stance in corpus linguistics that prioritizes data analysis over pre-existing hypotheses. This approach is often contrasted with corpus-based research, which relies on prior intuitions.

El término "corpus guiado" se utiliza principalmente para describir una postura metodológica en la lingüística de corpus que prioriza el análisis de datos sobre hipótesis preexistentes. Este enfoque a menudo se contrasta con la investigación basada en corpus, que se basa en intuiciones previas.

dataset

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento del lenguaje

Definition (EN)

A collection of data that can encompass various forms, including images, articles, or other objects, organized in a tabulated manner. Unlike a corpus, which contains a wide range of linguistic texts for analysis, a dataset is typically structured to represent specific variables in a defined format, often resembling a single database table. This distinction highlights the methodological differences between datasets and corpora, with the former being a subset of data that can be derived from the latter.

Definición (ES)

Un conjunto de datos que puede incluir diversas formas, como imágenes, artículos u otros objetos, organizados de manera tabulada. A diferencia de un corpus, que contiene una amplia gama de textos lingüísticos para su análisis, un dataset suele estar estructurado para representar variables específicas en un formato definido, asemejándose a una única tabla de base de datos. Esta distinción resalta las diferencias metodológicas entre los conjuntos de datos y los corpora, siendo el primero un subconjunto de datos que puede derivarse del segundo.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — A corpus is a broader collection of texts that can generate multiple datasets, whereas a dataset is a specific collection of data often derived from a corpus.
  • database — A database organizes information in a predefined structure for easy access, contrasting with a dataset, which may not have the same level of organization.
  • annotation — Datasets often require annotation to provide context or additional information about the data, similar to how corpora are annotated for linguistic analysis.
  • metadata — Metadata is crucial for datasets as it provides information about the data's characteristics, akin to how it is used in corpus linguistics to enhance the utility of the corpus.
  • corpus compilation — The process of corpus compilation can lead to the creation of various datasets, highlighting the relationship between these two concepts.
  • natural language processing — Datasets are frequently utilized in natural language processing tasks, serving as the foundation for training models and algorithms.
  • training corpus — A training corpus can be a source for creating datasets used in machine learning applications, emphasizing the practical application of both terms.

dependency parsing

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento del lenguaje

Definition (EN)

A method within natural language processing that involves the syntactic analysis of a sentence by establishing relationships between words, specifically identifying the dependencies between a head word and its dependents. This approach is essential for tasks such as semantic analysis and machine translation, as it provides a structured representation of sentence syntax. Dependency parsing contrasts with constituency parsing, which focuses on the hierarchical structure of phrases rather than the relationships between individual words.

Definición (ES)

El análisis de dependencias es un método de procesamiento del lenguaje natural que se centra en la identificación de las relaciones sintácticas entre las palabras de una oración, estableciendo qué palabras dependen de otras. Este enfoque es fundamental para tareas como el análisis semántico y la traducción automática, ya que ofrece una representación estructurada de la sintaxis de la oración. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

  • treebank — Dependency parsing results can be represented in treebanks, which provide a structured format for linguistic data.

descriptive statistics

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A branch of statistics that summarizes and describes the characteristics of a dataset, focusing on measures such as means, medians, and frequencies. This methodology is essential for interpreting nominal, ordinal, and cardinal data, as evidenced by its application in various statistical analyses within corpus linguistics. Descriptive statistics differ from inferential statistics, which aim to make predictions or inferences about a population based on sample data.

Definición (ES)

Una rama de la estadística que resume y describe las características de un conjunto de datos, centrándose en medidas como medias, medianas y frecuencias. Esta metodología es esencial para interpretar datos nominales, ordinales y cardinales, como se evidencia en su aplicación en diversos análisis estadísticos dentro de la lingüística de corpus. Las estadísticas descriptivas se diferencian de las estadísticas inferenciales, que buscan hacer predicciones o inferencias sobre una población a partir de datos de muestra.

  • mean score — The mean score is a key measure in descriptive statistics, providing an average value that summarizes a dataset.
  • standard deviation — Standard deviation is a descriptive statistic that quantifies the amount of variation or dispersion in a set of values.
  • inferential statistics — While descriptive statistics summarize data, inferential statistics use that summarized data to make predictions or generalizations about a larger population.
  • occurrence — Occurrence data is frequently analyzed using descriptive statistics to understand the frequency and distribution of specific items within a corpus.
  • sample size — The sample size is a critical factor in descriptive statistics, influencing the reliability and validity of the summarized data.
  • dataset — A dataset is the foundational element analyzed through descriptive statistics to extract meaningful insights about the data's characteristics.

diachronic corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A specialized collection of texts that captures linguistic changes over time, allowing for the analysis of language evolution. This type of corpus is distinguished from synchronic corpora by its ability to reflect chronological changes in form and content, thus providing insights into the dynamics of language as it develops. The methodological significance of diachronic corpora lies in their role in diachronic studies, which investigate how language properties evolve in relation to societal changes.

Definición (ES)

Colección especializada de textos que registra los cambios lingüísticos a lo largo del tiempo, permitiendo el análisis de la evolución del lenguaje. Este tipo de corpus se distingue de los corpus sincrónicos por su capacidad de reflejar cambios cronológicos en la forma y el contenido, proporcionando así información sobre la dinámica del lenguaje a medida que se desarrolla. La importancia metodológica de los corpus diacrónicos radica en su papel en los estudios diacrónicos, que investigan cómo evolucionan las propiedades del lenguaje en relación con los cambios sociales.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • synchronic — A diachronic corpus contrasts with a synchronic corpus, which focuses on a single period of language without considering historical changes.
  • corpus — A diachronic corpus is a specific type of corpus designed to study language change over time, as opposed to general corpora that may not have this temporal focus.
  • corpus design — The design of a diachronic corpus must account for the chronological and text-type diversity necessary for effective diachronic analysis.
  • historical corpus — A historical corpus is often synonymous with a diachronic corpus, as both aim to document language use across different time periods.

inferential statistics

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A branch of statistics that involves methods for making inferences about population parameters based on sample data. This approach is crucial for testing hypotheses and assessing the significance of observed effects, as evidenced by its application in evaluating evidence against the null hypothesis. Inferential statistics contrasts with descriptive statistics, which focuses solely on summarizing data without drawing conclusions about a larger population.

Definición (ES)

Una rama de la estadística que implica métodos para realizar inferencias sobre parámetros poblacionales basados en datos de muestra. Este enfoque es fundamental para la formulación de hipótesis y la evaluación de la significación de los efectos observados, tal como se evidencia en su aplicación para evaluar la evidencia contra la hipótesis nula. Las estadísticas inferenciales se contrastan con las estadísticas descriptivas, que se centran únicamente en resumir datos sin extraer conclusiones sobre una población más amplia.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • statistical significance — Inferential statistics often determines whether observed effects are statistically significant, providing a basis for rejecting or failing to reject the null hypothesis.
  • sample — A sample is the subset of data used in inferential statistics to make inferences about the larger population from which it is drawn.
  • probability — Probability theory underpins inferential statistics, as it provides the framework for making predictions and inferences based on sample data.
  • multivariate statistics — Multivariate statistics can be seen as an extension of inferential statistics, analyzing multiple variables simultaneously to draw conclusions about their interrelationships.

A specific type of annotation that is embedded directly within the text, allowing for the addition of interpretative information without altering the original content structure. This concept is crucial for assessing the reliability of annotation schemes, particularly in studies involving multiple categories, where discrepancies can arise due to ambiguity or vagueness in the guidelines. High inter-annotator agreement indicates that the annotation scheme is well-defined and can be reliably applied across different annotators.

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A measure of the degree of agreement among different annotators when assessing the same data set, indicating the consistency and reliability of the annotation process. This concept is critical in ensuring the quality of annotated data, as highlighted by the varying metrics used to calculate it, such as Cohen’s kappa and AC1, which address different aspects of agreement. The methodological status of this term is underscored by the ongoing debate regarding acceptable thresholds for reliability scores in annotation studies.

Este concepto es fundamental para garantizar la calidad de los datos anotados, y se utilizan diversas métricas para calcularlo, como el kappa de Cohen y AC1, que abordan diferentes aspectos del acuerdo. term_es: Corpus de habla académica de Michigan
html:
MICASE

Category / Categoría: Corpus de referencia

Definition (EN)

A specialized spoken language corpus, this resource comprises approximately 1.7 million words collected from nearly 190 hours of academic speech at the University of Michigan. It aims to capture the nuances of contemporary university discourse, providing empirical data for analyzing grammatical and phraseological patterns distinct from traditional written texts. The corpus serves as a foundational tool for researchers examining the evolution of academic speech within a diverse speaker population, including both native and non-native English speakers.

Definición (ES)

Un corpus de habla especializado que comprende aproximadamente 1.7 millones de palabras recolectadas de casi 190 horas de discurso académico en la Universidad de Michigan. Su objetivo es capturar las particularidades del discurso universitario contemporáneo, proporcionando datos empíricos para analizar patrones gramaticales y fraseológicos distintos de los textos escritos tradicionales. El corpus sirve como una herramienta fundamental para los investigadores que examinan la evolución del habla académica dentro de una población de hablantes diversa, que incluye tanto hablantes nativos como no nativos de inglés. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • speech corpus — MICASE is a specific example of a speech corpus, focusing on academic discourse.
  • academic speech — The corpus is designed to analyze the characteristics and patterns of academic speech in a university setting.
  • corpus design — The development of MICASE involved careful corpus design to ensure representativeness of various speaker demographics.
  • annotation — The corpus includes annotations that facilitate the analysis of linguistic features in academic speech.
  • corpus compilation — MICASE exemplifies the process of corpus compilation, gathering extensive spoken data for research purposes.
  • native speakers — The corpus includes contributions from both native and non-native speakers, highlighting linguistic diversity in academic contexts.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "In summary, Michigan Corpus of Academic Spoken English (MICASE) is a spoken language corpus of approximately 1.7 million words with duration of nearly 190 hours." (source)

  • "It was expected that once the investigators were able to examine the corpus for recurrent grammatical and phraseological patterns of use, they might find many divergences from those that were described in contemporary grammars and vocabulary books." (source)

  • "The MICASE corpus would provide authentic text materials in sufficient quantity to redefine the related concepts of academic speech." (source)

  • "Investigators would be able to track down generalized changes in speech patterns as people gain experience of university culture." (source)

  • "The speakers represented in the corpus include all faculty members, university staff, and all levels of students of both native and non-native English speakers." (source)

  • "With new data and information derived from the corpus, scholars would be in a better position to develop more appropriate texts for teaching English as a Second Language (ESL)." (source)

  • "To find answers to these questions, the first phase of the project started recording and transcribing nearly 200 hours of academic speech collected in the university." (source)

  • "The MICASE corpus was developed to provide a resource for empirical research on academic speech." (source)

  • "The corpus aimed to focus on the contemporary university speech of the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan." (source)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term MICASE is specifically tied to the study of academic spoken language, providing a unique resource for researchers interested in the dynamics of university discourse. Its design and compilation reflect a methodological approach that prioritizes the authenticity and diversity of academic speech patterns.

El término MICASE está vinculado específicamente al estudio del lenguaje hablado académico, proporcionando un recurso único para investigadores interesados en la dinámica del discurso universitario. Su diseño y compilación reflejan un enfoque metodológico que prioriza la autenticidad y diversidad de los patrones de habla académica.

monitor corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A specialized corpus that continuously grows over time, incorporating a wide variety of texts to reflect ongoing linguistic changes. Its primary function is to monitor language evolution by capturing new word usages and variations, thus serving as a dynamic resource for lexicographical studies. This contrasts with static corpora, which do not adapt to the changing linguistic landscape.

Definición (ES)

Un corpus especializado que crece continuamente a lo largo del tiempo, incorporando una amplia variedad de textos para reflejar los cambios lingüísticos en curso. Su función principal es monitorizar la evolución del lenguaje al capturar nuevos usos de palabras y variaciones, sirviendo así como un recurso dinámico para estudios lexicográficos. Esto contrasta con los corpus estáticos, que no se adaptan al paisaje lingüístico cambiante.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — A monitor corpus is a specific type of corpus designed for ongoing linguistic observation.
  • corpus design — The design of a monitor corpus involves principles that ensure continuous growth and representativeness over time.
  • reference corpus — Unlike a reference corpus, which is typically static, a monitor corpus is characterized by its dynamic nature and constant updates.
  • general corpus — A monitor corpus can be considered a subtype of general corpus, focusing specifically on language change and usage over time.
  • diachronic corpus — While a diachronic corpus examines language across different time periods, a monitor corpus does so in real-time, reflecting current usage trends.
  • corpus compilation — The process of compiling a monitor corpus requires specific methodologies to ensure it accurately reflects ongoing linguistic developments.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "A monitor corpus is a ‘representative corpus’ in the sense that it grows continuously with time to include infinite numbers and varieties of text samples from all possible sources of written and spoken the language to represent the language in its truest possible sense." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

  • "The primary purpose of a monitor corpus is to refer to the texts that are spoken or written in a language over a long time span." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

  • "Due to this quality, a monitor corpus has high functional relevance in lexicography since it captures the course of change of word use as well as constantly refurnishing new sets of data in order to trace the novel changes that are creeping into the language." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

  • "This particular aspect of a monitor corpus keeps untouched the relative balance of its components defined previously by pre-defined parameters." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

  • "The actual rate of flow of data into the corpus may be readjusted or monitored to address the demand for the changing features of a language." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

  • "Los corpus monitor buscan mostrar un estado actual de la lengua, de manera que contienen textos recientes, por decir algo, pertenecientes a los últimos 25 años." (2015_Sierra Martínez, G. E.)

  • "El corpus contiene un volumen textual o periodo de tiempo constantes, por lo que su contenido se actualiza con frecuencia." (2015_Sierra Martínez, G. E.)

  • "Esta acción ofrece la posibilidad de tener un corpus dinámico, en los que se van incluyendo nuevos materiales al mismo tiempo que se eliminan los más antiguos." (2015_Sierra Martínez, G. E.)

  • "El CREA es un ejemplo de corpus sincrónico contemporáneo, y el CORDE, por su parte, es un ejemplo de corpus diacrónico cronológico." (2015_Sierra Martínez, G. E.)

  • "El concepto de corpus monitor fue propuesto por Sinclair y se destina a monitorizar el cambio lingüístico." (2021_Rojo, G.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "monitor corpus" denotes a dynamic and evolving resource in corpus linguistics, emphasizing its role in tracking language change over time. Its definition and application may vary among scholars, particularly in relation to its contrast with static corpora and diachronic studies.

El término "corpus monitor" denota un recurso dinámico y en evolución en la lingüística de corpus, enfatizando su papel en el seguimiento del cambio lingüístico a lo largo del tiempo. Su definición y aplicación pueden variar entre los académicos, particularmente en relación con su contraste con los corpus estáticos y los estudios diacrónicos.

monolingual corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A collection of texts that belong to a single language, often designed to represent a specific variety or genre. Such corpora are utilized in linguistic studies to analyze language use within a defined context, contrasting with multilingual corpora that encompass multiple languages. The methodological focus on a single language allows for in-depth analysis of linguistic features and patterns.

Definición (ES)

Colección de textos que pertenecen a una única lengua, diseñada para representar una variedad o género específico. Estos corpus se utilizan en estudios lingüísticos para analizar el uso del lenguaje dentro de un contexto definido, en contraste con los corpus multilingües que abarcan múltiples lenguas. El enfoque metodológico en una sola lengua permite un análisis profundo de las características y patrones lingüísticos.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • multilingual corpus — A multilingual corpus includes texts from more than one language, contrasting with a monolingual corpus that focuses solely on one language.
  • parallel corpus — A parallel corpus consists of texts that are translations of each other, while a monolingual corpus contains texts in only one language.
  • reference corpus — A reference corpus is often monolingual and serves as a general resource for various linguistic studies.
  • sample corpus — A sample corpus can be a type of monolingual corpus, representing a specific subset of a larger linguistic population.
  • general corpus — A general corpus may be monolingual and is designed for broad linguistic analysis across various contexts.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • Typically, reference corpora target a single language, often a standard and/or official language of a nation-state (German, Turkish, Russian, etc.). Such corpora are thus monolingual. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • Monolingual versus multilingual corpora. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • Corpus constituido por textos pertenecientes a un solo período de una lengua. (2021_Rojo, G._Introducción a la lingüística de corpus en español)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "monolingual corpus" is widely accepted in corpus linguistics, emphasizing the focus on a single language for analysis. However, its application may vary depending on the specific linguistic context or research objectives.

El término "corpus monolingüe" es ampliamente aceptado en la lingüística de corpus, enfatizando el enfoque en una sola lengua para el análisis. Sin embargo, su aplicación puede variar según el contexto lingüístico específico o los objetivos de investigación.

morphological annotation

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A specific type of linguistic annotation that captures the morphological features of tokens within a corpus, including aspects such as number, gender, and tense. This annotation is essential for enabling systematic analysis of linguistic data across different layers of information. Morphological annotation is often part of a broader annotation scheme that may include syntactic and semantic layers, distinguishing it from simpler forms of annotation like tokenization.

Definición (ES)

La anotación morfológica es un tipo de anotación lingüística que se centra en capturar las características morfológicas de los tokens dentro de un corpus, como el número, el género y el tiempo verbal. Este tipo de anotación es fundamental para permitir un análisis sistemático de los datos lingüísticos a través de diferentes capas de información. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — Morphological annotation is a specific type of annotation that focuses on morphological features.
  • part-of-speech tagging — Morphological annotation often includes part-of-speech tagging as a component of its analysis.
  • syntactic annotation — While morphological annotation deals with word forms, syntactic annotation addresses the relationships between those forms.
  • annotated corpus — An annotated corpus typically includes morphological annotations among other types of linguistic information.
  • treebank — Treebanks may incorporate morphological annotations to represent hierarchical dependencies in sentence structures.

  • It is also on this level that clause boundaries are inserted that mark the beginning of clauses, represented by ‘##’ or ‘#’, depending on the type of clause. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S.)

  • The structure of the different layers of annotation is organised in such a way that the top layer is time-aligned, with the segment roughly representing what annotators identify as an IU. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

Morphological annotation is crucial in corpus linguistics for analyzing the grammatical properties of words, facilitating deeper linguistic insights. Its integration with other annotation types enhances the richness of linguistic data, allowing for comprehensive analyses across various linguistic dimensions.

La anotación morfológica es fundamental en la lingüística de corpus para analizar las propiedades gramaticales de las palabras, facilitando una comprensión lingüística más profunda. Su integración con otros tipos de anotación enriquece los datos lingüísticos, permitiendo análisis exhaustivos a través de diversas dimensiones lingüísticas.

multilingual corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A collection of texts in multiple languages, typically designed for comparative linguistic analysis or translation studies. This type of corpus may include parallel texts, where original and translated versions are aligned, or comparable texts that share similar topics or genres but are not direct translations. The methodological significance of multilingual corpora is highlighted in their role in enhancing cross-linguistic research and developing language processing tools.

Definición (ES)

Conjunto de textos que pertenecen a varias lenguas, diseñado generalmente para el análisis lingüístico comparativo o los estudios de traducción. Este tipo de corpus puede incluir textos paralelos, donde se alinean versiones originales y traducidas, o textos comparables que comparten temas o géneros similares pero no son traducciones directas. La importancia metodológica de los corpus multilingües radica en su capacidad para mejorar la investigación en lingüística contrastiva y en el desarrollo de herramientas de procesamiento del lenguaje.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • parallel corpus — A type of multilingual corpus that specifically contains texts that are translations of each other.
  • comparable corpus — A related concept that refers to multilingual corpora consisting of texts that are not translations but are similar in topic or genre.
  • corpus compilation — The process involved in creating multilingual corpora, emphasizing the need for careful selection and alignment of texts.
  • translation corpus — A subset of multilingual corpora focused specifically on texts and their translations, often used in translation studies.
  • corpus design — The methodological framework guiding the creation of multilingual corpora, ensuring representativeness and alignment.
  • corpus annotation — A crucial step in processing multilingual corpora, involving the addition of linguistic information to the texts.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "In order to achieve this objective, the corpus has to meet certain requirements regarding quality of texts and translations, size and representativeness and accuracy of the alignment." (2017_Doval, I.)

  • "Se diferencia habitualmente entre los corpus paralelos, que contienen textos que son traducciones unos de otros, y los corpus comparables, que contienen textos diferentes." (2021_Rojo, G.)

  • "Este tipo de corpus puede incluir textos paralelos, donde se alinean versiones originales y traducidas, o textos comparables que comparten temas o géneros similares." (2021_Rojo, G.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "multilingual corpus" encompasses a variety of corpus types, including parallel and comparable corpora, which serve different research purposes. While the definitions and applications may vary, the overarching goal remains the facilitation of cross-linguistic analysis and the enhancement of translation studies.

El término "corpus multilingüe" abarca una variedad de tipos de corpus, incluidos los corpus paralelos y comparables, que sirven a diferentes propósitos de investigación. Si bien las definiciones y aplicaciones pueden variar, el objetivo general sigue siendo la facilitación del análisis contrastivo y la mejora de los estudios de traducción.

multimodal corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A specialized collection that integrates various modes of human communication, including spoken and written texts, gestures, and visual elements. This type of corpus is designed to provide a comprehensive representation of communication by aligning transcripts with audio or video recordings, thus addressing the limitations of traditional text and speech corpora. The methodological focus on multimodal interaction allows for in-depth analysis of the interplay between verbal and non-verbal communication features.

Definición (ES)

Un corpus especializado que integra diferentes modalidades de comunicación humana, incluyendo textos hablados y escritos, gestos y elementos visuales. Este tipo de corpus está diseñado para proporcionar una representación integral de la comunicación al alinear transcripciones con grabaciones de audio o video, abordando así las limitaciones de los corpus de texto y de habla tradicionales. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotated corpus — A multimodal corpus is a specific type of annotated corpus that includes multiple forms of data beyond text.
  • speech corpus — Unlike a speech corpus, which focuses solely on spoken language, a multimodal corpus encompasses both verbal and non-verbal communication.
  • corpus design — The creation of a multimodal corpus requires careful corpus design to ensure the integration of various modalities.
  • metadata — Metadata in a multimodal corpus is crucial for understanding the context and structure of the diverse data types included.
  • corpus compilation — The process of corpus compilation for multimodal corpora involves unique challenges due to the need for synchronization of different data types.
  • annotation scheme — A multimodal corpus necessitates a robust annotation scheme that accommodates the complexity of multiple communication channels.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • A recent offshoot in the field of corpus typology is a multimodal corpus, which records and annotates several modalities of human communication and aims to include spoken texts, written texts, gestures, hand movements, facial expressions, body postures and so on.   • The combination of textual, audio and video data of various communicative events in multimodal corpus provides “a unique source for the exploration of a range of lexical, prosodic and gestural features of conversation, and for investigations of the ways in which these features interact in real, everyday speech.” (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

  • It has been acknowledged that one shortcoming of spoken corpora is that they lack visual representations by showing speech in textual format, which the multimodal approach is attempting to tackle, by depicting communication in its ‘entire complexity.’ (2016_Murphy, B., Riordan, E._Corpus types and uses)

  • The basic focus of the enterprise for multimodal corpus generation is directed towards the techniques of non-verbal communication studies and their contribution to the definition of the collection of protocols, coding schemes, inter-annotator agreement measures, and reliable models of exploring multimodal behaviors in communication. (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

  • Such a corpus is considered particularly valuable in communication studies. (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

  • The origin of the multimodal corpus was triggered from the limitations of text and speech corpora. (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "multimodal corpus" is still developing within the field of corpus linguistics, with ongoing discussions about its definition and scope. Its emergence reflects a growing recognition of the need to analyze communication in a more holistic manner, incorporating both verbal and non-verbal elements.

El término "corpus multimodal" está en desarrollo dentro del campo de la lingüística de corpus, con discusiones en curso sobre su definición y alcance. Su aparición refleja un reconocimiento creciente de la necesidad de analizar la comunicación de manera más holística, incorporando tanto elementos verbales como no verbales.

mutual information

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure of co-occurrence that quantifies the degree to which the presence of one word influences the presence of another word. This measure is grounded in information theory and is commonly employed in corpus linguistics to assess collocational strength. It is methodologically significant, as it provides a standard for evaluating the association between lexemes, contrasting with other measures like Fisher’s exact test or chi-squared.

Definición (ES)

Una medida estadística de coocurrencia que cuantifica el grado en que la presencia de una palabra influye en la presencia de otra. Este concepto, fundamentado en la teoría de la información, se utiliza frecuentemente en la lingüística de corpus para evaluar la fuerza de las colocaciones. Su importancia metodológica radica en que ofrece un estándar para evaluar la asociación entre lexemas, en contraste con otras medidas como la prueba exacta de Fisher o el chi-cuadrado.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • association measures — Mutual information is one of several association measures used to evaluate the strength of relationships between words.
  • collocation — This term is closely related as mutual information specifically measures the strength of collocations.
  • Fisher’s exact test — Unlike mutual information, Fisher’s exact test assesses the association between two lexemes under the assumption of independence.
  • chi-squared — Both chi-squared and mutual information are used to analyze word associations, but they employ different statistical methodologies.
  • probability — Mutual information relies on the probabilities of word occurrences to determine the strength of their association.
  • keyword analysis — In keyword analysis, mutual information can be used to identify significant word pairs that co-occur more frequently than expected.

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "mutual information" is widely recognized in corpus linguistics as a standard measure for assessing word associations, particularly in collocation studies. Variations in its application may arise from differing methodological approaches or the specific contexts in which it is employed.

El término "información mutua" es ampliamente reconocido en la lingüística de corpus como una medida estándar para evaluar las asociaciones entre palabras, especialmente en estudios de colocaciones. Las variaciones en su aplicación pueden surgir de diferentes enfoques metodológicos o de los contextos específicos en los que se emplea.

n-gram

Category / Categoría: Léxico y fraseología

Definition (EN)

A sequence of n words occurring in a specific order within a text, where n can be any integer greater than one. This term is commonly applied in natural language processing and corpus linguistics to analyze patterns and predict word sequences. Unlike unigrams or bigrams, which refer specifically to one or two words, n-grams encompass a broader range of word combinations, making them useful for various computational tasks.

Definición (ES)

Una secuencia de n palabras que ocurren en un orden específico dentro de un texto, donde n puede ser cualquier número entero mayor que uno. Este término se aplica comúnmente en el procesamiento del lenguaje natural y la lingüística de corpus para analizar patrones y predecir secuencias de palabras. NOW Corpus

Category / Categoría: Corpus de referencia

Definition (EN)

A collection of web-based texts that serves as a large-scale resource for linguistic analysis, characterized by its extensive size and the diversity of its content. This corpus is utilized for various research purposes, including the study of language use across different contexts and genres, contrasting with smaller, more specialized corpora. The NOW Corpus exemplifies the methodological shift towards using digital platforms for corpus linguistics, reflecting the growing importance of web corpora in contemporary linguistic research.

Definición (ES)

Una colección de textos basados en la web que sirve como un recurso a gran escala para el análisis lingüístico, caracterizada por su tamaño extenso y la diversidad de su contenido. Este corpus se utiliza para diversos propósitos de investigación, incluyendo el estudio del uso del lenguaje en diferentes contextos y géneros, en contraste con corpus más pequeños y especializados. El Corpus NOW ejemplifica el cambio metodológico hacia el uso de plataformas digitales en la lingüística de corpus, reflejando la creciente importancia de los corpus web en la investigación lingüística contemporánea.

  • general corpus — The NOW Corpus functions as a general corpus, encompassing a wide range of texts rather than focusing on a specialized domain.
  • corpus compilation — The creation of the NOW Corpus involves corpus compilation techniques that gather and organize web texts for research purposes.
  • BNC — The NOW Corpus can be contrasted with the British National Corpus (BNC), which is a more traditional, structured corpus of British English.
  • corpus design — The design of the NOW Corpus reflects contemporary methodologies in corpus linguistics, particularly in terms of digital text collection.

occurrence

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A measurable event that signifies the presence of a specific item within a given text or corpus. This term is often utilized in statistical analyses to quantify how frequently an item appears relative to the total number of tokens, thereby providing insights into its significance within the text. The concept is essential for understanding dispersion measures and frequency distributions in corpus linguistics.

Definición (ES)

Un evento medible que indica la presencia de un ítem específico dentro de un texto o corpus determinado. Este término se utiliza frecuentemente en análisis estadísticos para cuantificar la frecuencia con la que un ítem aparece en relación con el número total de tokens, proporcionando así información sobre su relevancia dentro del texto. Es fundamental para comprender las medidas de dispersión y las distribuciones de frecuencia en la lingüística de corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • frequency — Occurrence is a key component in calculating frequency, which measures how often an item appears in a corpus.
  • token — Each occurrence corresponds to a token, which is a single instance of a word or item in a text.
  • dispersion — The concept of occurrence is crucial for analyzing dispersion, as it helps to assess how evenly an item is distributed across different texts.
  • corpus — Occurrences are counted within a corpus, making it a foundational concept in corpus linguistics.
  • normalized frequency — This term relates to occurrence as it adjusts the raw count of occurrences to account for varying text lengths, allowing for more accurate comparisons.

parallel corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

Collections of texts in one language aligned with their translations in another language characterize this type of corpus. They are utilized extensively in contrastive linguistics and translation studies, often requiring expert translations to ensure quality. The term is sometimes ambiguously used, as it can also refer to comparable original texts, but it is distinct in its focus on aligned bitexts.

Definición (ES)

Conjuntos de textos originales en una lengua, alineados con sus traducciones en otra lengua, definen este tipo de corpus. Se utilizan ampliamente en la lingüística contrastiva y en estudios de traducción, y suelen requerir traducciones realizadas por expertos para garantizar la calidad. Aunque el término puede usarse de manera ambigua, se distingue por su enfoque en los textos alineados.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • comparable corpus — This term refers to collections of original texts in one language that are similar in content to texts translated into another language, contrasting with the aligned nature of parallel corpora.
  • corpus annotation — The process of adding linguistic information to the texts in a parallel corpus is essential for enhancing the analysis of translation and linguistic features.
  • translation studies — Parallel corpora are a fundamental resource in this field, providing empirical data for examining translation practices and strategies.
  • multilingual corpus — While a parallel corpus typically involves two languages, a multilingual corpus encompasses multiple languages, often including parallel texts as a subset.
  • corpus compilation — The creation of a parallel corpus involves specific methodologies for selecting, aligning, and annotating texts, making it a specialized area within corpus compilation.
  • POS tagging — This technique is often applied to parallel corpora to analyze the grammatical structures of both source and target languages.
  • natural language processing — Parallel corpora serve as crucial datasets for developing algorithms and tools in this field, particularly for machine translation applications.

parsing

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento del lenguaje

Definition (EN)

The process of syntactic analysis involves the application of algorithms to determine the grammatical structure of sentences, resulting in parse trees that represent the syntactic relationships among words. This methodology can be executed through both manual and automated means, with the latter increasingly relying on statistical approaches to enhance accuracy. Parsing is essential for extracting syntactic information from corpora, which is necessary for advanced linguistic analysis and applications.

Definición (ES)

El análisis sintáctico consiste en la aplicación de algoritmos para determinar la estructura gramatical de las oraciones, generando árboles de análisis que representan las relaciones sintácticas entre las palabras. Este proceso puede llevarse a cabo mediante métodos manuales o automáticos, siendo estos últimos cada vez más dependientes de enfoques estadísticos para mejorar la precisión. El análisis sintáctico es fundamental para extraer información sintáctica de los corpus, lo cual es necesario para análisis lingüísticos avanzados y aplicaciones.

  • treebank — Parsed corpora are often referred to as treebanks, which contain syntactic annotations in tree structure formats.
  • annotation — The process of parsing is a form of annotation that adds syntactic information to textual data.
  • dependency parsing — A specific type of parsing that focuses on the dependencies between words in a sentence, contrasting with phrase-structure parsing.
  • corpus annotation — Parsing is a critical component of corpus annotation, providing necessary syntactic insights for linguistic research.
  • syntax — Parsing directly relates to syntax, as it involves analyzing the grammatical structure of sentences.

part-of-speech tagging

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A process within corpus linguistics that involves assigning a part-of-speech label to each token in a text based on its form and context. This method consists of two main steps: tag assignment, where possible tags are assigned, and tag disambiguation, which reduces the tags to the correct one for the specific context. The complexity of this task arises from the inherent ambiguity of word forms, making it challenging even for human annotators without complete syntactic analysis.

Definición (ES)

Proceso en la lingüística de corpus que consiste en asignar una etiqueta de parte del discurso a cada token en un texto, basándose en su forma y contexto. Este procedimiento incluye dos etapas principales: la asignación de etiquetas, donde se asignan las posibles etiquetas, y la desambiguación de etiquetas, que reduce las etiquetas a la correcta para el contexto específico. La ambigüedad inherente de las formas de palabras complica esta tarea, dificultando su realización incluso para los anotadores humanos sin un análisis sintáctico completo.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — Part-of-speech tagging is a specific type of annotation that enriches textual data with grammatical information.
  • token — Tokens are the individual elements to which part-of-speech tags are assigned during the tagging process.
  • tagset — The set of possible tags used in part-of-speech tagging defines the categories into which tokens can be classified.
  • morphological annotation — Part-of-speech tagging is a form of morphological annotation that focuses specifically on the grammatical role of words.
  • corpus annotation — Part-of-speech tagging is a crucial component of corpus annotation, contributing to the overall analysis of linguistic data.
  • tagger — A tagger is the tool or algorithm used to perform part-of-speech tagging on a given text.
