parts of speech

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A grammatical category that classifies words based on their function within a sentence, such as nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs. This classification is essential for understanding syntactic structures and is often utilized in corpus linguistics for tasks like part-of-speech tagging. The term is methodologically significant as it aids in the analysis of linguistic data and the identification of patterns in language use.

Definición (ES)

Categoría gramatical que clasifica las palabras según su función dentro de una oración, como sustantivos, verbos, adjetivos y adverbios. Esta clasificación es fundamental para comprender las estructuras sintácticas y se utiliza frecuentemente en la lingüística de corpus para tareas como el etiquetado de partes del discurso. El término tiene un estatus metodológico significativo, ya que facilita el análisis de datos lingüísticos y la identificación de patrones en el uso del lenguaje.

Penn Treebank

Category / Categoría: Corpus de referencia

Definition (EN)

A syntactically annotated corpus that serves as a standard for part-of-speech tagging and syntactic parsing in English. It provides a framework for analyzing the grammatical structure of sentences, facilitating various linguistic studies and applications in computational linguistics. The methodology established by the Penn Treebank has influenced the development of other tagging systems and treebanks across different languages.

Definición (ES)

Un corpus anotado sintácticamente que sirve como estándar para el etiquetado de partes del discurso y el análisis sintáctico en inglés. Proporciona un marco para analizar la estructura gramatical de las oraciones, facilitando diversos estudios lingüísticos y aplicaciones en lingüística computacional. La metodología establecida por el Penn Treebank ha influido en el desarrollo de otros sistemas de etiquetado y treebanks en diferentes lenguas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • tagset — The Penn Treebank employs a specific tagset for part-of-speech tagging, which has become a reference for other tagging systems.
  • syntactic annotation — The corpus is a prime example of syntactic annotation, providing detailed grammatical structures for linguistic analysis.
  • annotated corpus — It is classified as an annotated corpus due to its extensive syntactic and part-of-speech tagging.
  • dependency parsing — While the Penn Treebank primarily uses constituency parsing, it has influenced the development of dependency parsing frameworks.
  • corpus design — The design of the Penn Treebank has set a precedent for the creation of other specialized corpora in various languages.
  • grammar — The corpus is instrumental in studying English grammar through its detailed syntactic annotations.

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A process within corpus linguistics that involves assigning part-of-speech labels to tokens in a text, based on their form and context. It is a crucial preprocessing step in natural language processing applications and is essential for effective corpus data exploitation.

Definición (ES)

Este método incluye dos pasos principales: la asignación de etiquetas, donde se asignan las posibles etiquetas, y la desambiguación de etiquetas, que reduce las opciones a la etiqueta correcta para cada token. Es un paso de preprocesamiento crucial en aplicaciones de procesamiento del lenguaje natural y es esencial para la explotación efectiva de los datos del corpus.

raw frequency

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure representing the total number of occurrences of a specific item within a corpus, raw frequency does not account for the overall size of the corpus or the relative significance of the occurrences. This term is often contrasted with relative frequency, which provides a proportionate view of occurrences in relation to the total number of items. Methodologically, raw frequency can be misleading if used without consideration of other statistical measures, as it may not accurately reflect the importance of the data in linguistic analysis.

Definición (ES)

Una medida cuantitativa que representa el número total de ocurrencias de un ítem específico dentro de un corpus, la frecuencia bruta no toma en cuenta el tamaño total del corpus ni la significación relativa de las ocurrencias. Este término se contrasta a menudo con la frecuencia relativa, que ofrece una visión proporcional de las ocurrencias en relación con el número total de ítems. Metodológicamente, la frecuencia bruta puede resultar engañosa si se utiliza sin considerar otras medidas estadísticas, ya que puede no reflejar con precisión la importancia de los datos en el análisis lingüístico.

  • corpus — The corpus serves as the foundational dataset from which raw frequencies are derived, emphasizing the context in which the term is applied.
  • absolute frequency — This term is synonymous with raw frequency, both indicating the total count of occurrences without normalization.
  • normalized frequency — Normalized frequency adjusts raw frequency to account for corpus size, providing a more accurate representation of item significance.

recall

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A measure of the effectiveness of a retrieval method, calculated as the number of true positives divided by the sum of true positives and false negatives. This metric indicates the proportion of relevant instances that were successfully identified, highlighting the completeness of the search results. Recall is often contrasted with precision, which focuses on the accuracy of the retrieved items.

La recuperación se contrasta frecuentemente con la precisión, que se centra en la exactitud de los elementos recuperados.

Definition (EN)

This contrasts with a learner corpus, which focuses specifically on language produced by learners rather than a comprehensive linguistic representation.

Esto contrasta con un corpus de aprendices, que se centra específicamente en el lenguaje producido por los aprendices en lugar de una representación lingüística integral.

relative frequency

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure that expresses the frequency of a linguistic phenomenon as a proportion of the total number of occurrences within a defined sample or corpus. This calculation is achieved by dividing the absolute frequency of the phenomenon by the total number of cases, allowing for comparisons across different datasets. The methodological significance of relative frequency lies in its ability to normalize data, thereby facilitating more accurate analyses of linguistic patterns.

La importancia metodológica de la frecuencia relativa radica en su capacidad para normalizar los datos, facilitando así análisis más precisos de los patrones lingüísticos.

  • normalized frequency — Relative frequency is often used interchangeably with normalized frequency, though the latter may imply additional adjustments for comparability.
  • sample size — The accuracy of relative frequency calculations is influenced by the sample size from which the absolute frequencies are derived.

sample size

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure representing the number of texts or data points included in a corpus, which is essential for achieving reliable estimates of linguistic parameters. Los corpus especializados son especialmente útiles para la investigación lingüística dirigida, ya que permiten examinar características del lenguaje que pueden no ser prevalentes en conjuntos de datos más amplios.

Definition (EN)

A collection of spoken language data, typically transcribed or recorded, used for linguistic analysis and research. This type of corpus is essential for studying phonetics, speech recognition, and discourse analysis, as it captures the nuances of natural spoken interaction. The generation of speech corpora is often more complex than that of written corpora due to the inherent variability and spontaneity of spoken language.

standard deviation

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure of dispersion, this value quantifies the extent to which individual data points differ from the mean of a dataset. It is calculated as the square root of the variance, which itself is derived from the average of the squared differences between each data point and the mean. The standard deviation is widely utilized in corpus linguistics to assess variability in frequency distributions, although it may not be ideal for skewed data distributions.

Definición (ES)

Medida estadística de la dispersión, este valor cuantifica el grado en que los puntos de datos individuales difieren de la media de un conjunto de datos. Se calcula como la raíz cuadrada de la varianza, que a su vez se deriva del promedio de las diferencias al cuadrado entre cada punto de datos y la media. La desviación estándar se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para evaluar la variabilidad en las distribuciones de frecuencia, aunque puede no ser ideal para distribuciones de datos sesgadas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • frequency — Standard deviation is often used to analyze frequency distributions, providing insight into the variability of occurrences.
  • sample size — The calculation of standard deviation is influenced by sample size, as a larger sample can lead to a more accurate estimate of variability.
  • confidence interval — The standard deviation plays a crucial role in determining the width of confidence intervals in statistical analyses.
  • descriptive statistics — Standard deviation is a key component of descriptive statistics, summarizing the spread of data points in a dataset.
  • probability — Understanding standard deviation is essential for interpreting probabilities associated with normal distributions.

statistical significance

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A measure indicating that the results obtained from a sample are unlikely to have occurred by chance, thus allowing for generalization to the broader population. Statistical significance is distinct from theoretical importance, as it does not imply the strength or relevance of the observed relationship. It is essential in research methodology to ensure that findings are not merely random occurrences.

Definición (ES)

Una medida que indica que los resultados obtenidos de una muestra son poco probables que hayan ocurrido por azar, lo que permite su generalización a la población más amplia. La significancia estadística se distingue de la importancia teórica, ya que no implica la fuerza o relevancia de la relación observada. Es esencial en la metodología de investigación para asegurar que los hallazgos no son meras ocurrencias aleatorias.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • probability — Statistical significance relies on probability calculations to determine the likelihood that results are due to chance.
  • effect size — While statistical significance indicates whether an effect exists, effect size measures the magnitude of that effect.
  • inferential statistics — Statistical significance is a key concept within inferential statistics, which aims to draw conclusions about populations based on sample data.
  • confidence interval — A confidence interval provides a range of values that likely contain the population parameter, complementing the notion of statistical significance.
  • chi-squared — The chi-squared test is commonly used to assess statistical significance in categorical data analysis.
  • sample size — The size of the sample can influence the statistical significance of the results, with larger samples often yielding more reliable significance levels.

Definition (EN)

A lexical item characterized by its high frequency and low semantic content, often excluded from analyses to enhance the clarity of keyword identification. The methodological use of stopwords is evident in corpus linguistics, where they are filtered out to improve the quality of topic modeling and keyword analysis. This contrasts with content words, which carry significant meaning and are crucial for understanding the text's subject matter.

Definición (ES)

Su uso metodológico es habitual en la lingüística de corpus, donde se filtran para mejorar la calidad del modelado de temas y el análisis de palabras clave. Se distinguen de las palabras de contenido, que poseen significado referencial y resultan fundamentales para comprender el tema del texto.

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definición (ES)

Una categoría de palabras que comparten propiedades gramaticales similares, diferenciadas por sus funciones sintácticas y morfológicas dentro de una oración. Esta clasificación es esencial para la anotación morfosintáctica, ya que influye en el significado y el uso de las formas de palabras en diversos contextos. word frequency

Category / Categoría: Léxico y fraseología

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure indicating how often specific word forms appear within a given text or corpus. This metric is essential for generating frequency lists, which can be sorted to reveal patterns in language use, such as identifying the most common or least common words. The methodology for calculating word frequency often involves tokenization and normalization processes to ensure accuracy across different corpora.

Definición (ES)

Una medida cuantitativa que indica con qué frecuencia aparecen formas específicas de palabras dentro de un texto o corpus determinado. Este concepto es fundamental para generar listas de frecuencia, que pueden ordenarse para revelar patrones en el uso del lenguaje, como la identificación de las palabras más comunes o menos comunes. La metodología para calcular la frecuencia de palabras a menudo implica procesos de segmentación y normalización para garantizar la precisión en diferentes corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • frequency list — A frequency list is a compilation of word types along with their respective frequencies, derived from the analysis of word frequency.

  • raw frequency — Raw frequency refers to the total count of occurrences of a word form, which is a foundational component in determining word frequency.
  • normalized frequency — Normalized frequency adjusts raw frequency based on the size of the corpus, providing a more meaningful comparison of word frequency across different texts.
  • stopword — Stopwords are often excluded from frequency counts, as they typically contribute little to the semantic content of a text, contrasting with the focus on significant word frequency.
  • lemma — A lemma is the base form of a word, and its frequency can be analyzed to understand the usage of different inflected forms within a corpus.

A markup language that allows users to define their own tags, facilitating the creation of structured documents. XML enhances the separation of content from presentation, enabling better organization and retrieval of information within corpora. It is often contrasted with HTML, which is more rigid in its predefined tags and structure.

z-score

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure that describes a value's relation to the mean of a group of values, expressed in terms of standard deviations. This metric is essential in quantitative linguistics for assessing the significance of linguistic features within a corpus. Unlike raw scores, z-scores standardize data, allowing for comparisons across different datasets or distributions.

Definición (ES)

Una medida estadística que describe la relación de un valor con la media de un grupo de valores, expresada en términos de desviaciones estándar. Este concepto es fundamental en la lingüística cuantitativa para evaluar la significación de características lingüísticas dentro de un corpus. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

  • statistical significance — Z-scores are crucial in determining the statistical significance of results in linguistic studies.
